# Inference on single prop

$p$ = proportion of prosocial choices chimp A makes with a partner

X = number of prosocial choices Chimp A makes with a partner $\sim Binom(90, p)$


(We assume that X satisfies BINS assumptions but S might not be satisfied here).

```{r}
x = 60 # number of successes
n = 90 # number of trials

# Normal model of testing
phat = x/n

se_w = sqrt(phat*(1-phat)/n) # wald estimate

# 95% ci for the prop of prosocial choice that Chimp a makes

cv = qnorm(0.975)

phat + c(-1, 1)*cv*se_w

# Normal model hypo testing for p
# H0: p = 0.5, H_alpha: p < 0.5

z = (phat-0.5)/se_w
z # lies in the right hand side

p_val = pnorm(z, lower.tail = F) # right tailed p value
p_val

pnorm(z) # left tailed p-value

# alpha = 0.05, p-val < alpha, We have sufficient evidence to support the claim that Chimp A is making prosocial choices
```


# Diff of prop

$p_1 = \text{Proportion of prosocial choices when Chimp A has no partner}$ (true p1 should be around 0.5 or random choices)

$p_2 = \text{Proportion of prosocial choices when Chimp A has a partner}$ (true p2 should be more than 0.5 or prosocial choices)

parameter: $p_1-p_2$
p.e: $\hat{p}_1- \hat{p}_2$
se_adj:

CI: $$\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_1(1- \hat{p}_1)}{n_1}+ \frac{\hat{p}_2(1- \hat{p}_2)}{n_2}}$$



Hypo test: $$\sqrt{\frac{\tilde{p}(1- \tilde{p})}{n_1}+ \frac{\tilde{p}(1- \tilde{p})}{n_2}}$$

$$H_0: p_1-p_2 = 0 \\ H_{\alpha}: p_1-p_2 < 0$$



```{r}
x1 = 16
n1 = 30
x2 = 60 
n2 = 90

phat1 = x1/n1
phat2 = x2/n2
ptilde = (x1+x2)/(n1+n2) # global prop

cv = qnorm(0.975)

se_ci = sqrt((phat1*(1-phat1)/n1)+(phat2*(1-phat2)/n2)) # se for CI


# 95% CI for p1-p2
(phat1-phat2) + c(-1,1)*cv*se_ci # note that the CI includes 0, which means that monkey makes prosocial choices irrespective of the presence of a partner


se_ht = sqrt((ptilde*(1-ptilde)*(1/n1+ 1/n2))) # se for hypothesis testing
             
z = (phat1-phat2)/se_ht # test statistic

pnorm(z) # p-val and comparing it with alpha = 0.05, we fail to reject H_0, whihc also coincides with the 95% CI built earlier
```
